entity_name: Bridger-Teton National Forest — Mineral Entry & Rockhounding Research Guide

entity_name: McCullough Peaks WSA — Named BLM Rockhounding
public_reason: BLM currently names rock hounding and notes paleontological/geologic interest. Split-estate and state acreage, active rights and fossil-class rules prevent blanket collecting recommendations.

entity_name: Cedar Mountain WSA — Petrified Wood & Fossil Research Explainer
public_reason: BLM documents petrified wood plus vertebrate fossil occurrence. Vertebrate fossils are protected, and special-area/local collecting authority for petrified wood must be verified before field recommendation.

entity_name: Hartville Uplift — Agate & Jasper Research Explainer
public_reason: WSGS documents diverse agate and jasper occurrence in the Hartville uplift, but geology does not resolve present parcel ownership, mineral rights, claims or lawful collecting footprint.

entity_name: BLM Developed Recreation Site Collection Exclusion
public_reason: Current BLM guidance says ordinary rock collection is generally not allowed at developed recreation sites and other specially restricted areas.

entity_name: BLM MLRS — Live Mining-Claim Screen Control
public_reason: MLRS is the current BLM platform for mineral and land records. Field destinations that can overlap locatable-mineral claims must receive a current MLRS/case screen before a collect-now recommendation.

entity_name: BLM Private Mineral Estate / Split-Estate Firewall
public_reason: General BLM surface access never establishes a right to remove privately owned minerals or material subject to another authorized mineral use.

entity_name: BLM Public Lands Access Data — Legal Access Control
public_reason: PLAD identifies legal access to BLM-managed land across easements/reservations. A mapped access route proves only legal passage to BLM land and never authorizes collecting or other use on crossed non-BLM land.

entity_name: BLM Wyoming Fossil Class Rule
public_reason: Vertebrate fossils cannot be casually collected; common invertebrate and plant fossils may be collected in reasonable personal-use quantities where local restrictions allow.

entity_name: BLM Wyoming Gemstone & Common Mineral Personal-Use Rule
public_reason: Reasonable personal-use gemstone/common mineral specimen collection is allowed on eligible BLM lands; large quantities/resale require authorization.

entity_name: BLM Wyoming General Recreational Rockhounding Rule
public_reason: Nearly all BLM Wyoming public lands allow limited noncommercial rock material collection subject to local restrictions and rights.

entity_name: BLM Wyoming Mining Claim Material-Matching Guard
public_reason: On an unpatented claim, casual collectors must not interfere with mining or collect the locatable mineral for which the claim is located; patented claims are private land.

entity_name: BLM Wyoming Petrified Wood Quantity Rule
public_reason: Eligible BLM petrified wood casual collection is limited to 25 pounds plus one piece per day and 250 pounds per calendar year without a permit.

entity_name: Trust Engine — Source Drift Activity Signal Control

entity_name: Wyoming BLM High Desert District 2026 Stage 1 Fire Control
public_reason: Current BLM fire page lists a July 2026 Stage 1 order for Teton, Sublette, Lincoln, Uinta, Sweetwater, Fremont, Carbon, Albany and Laramie counties; this is a trip restriction, not collecting authority.

entity_name: Wyoming State Trust Fossil Permit Control
public_reason: OSLI uses commercial and scientific fossil-removal permits; a recreational visitor cannot infer fossil-removal authority from surface access.

entity_name: Wyoming State Trust Solid-Mineral Authority Control
public_reason: OSLI administers leases for solid minerals including precious stones, sand and gravel; casual public-land rules are not inherited onto State Trust mineral interests.

entity_name: BLM Wyoming Abandoned Mine Lands — No Entry Safety Control
public_reason: BLM Wyoming says abandoned mine lands should not be entered under any circumstance.

entity_name: BLM Wyoming Cave Resources — No Removal Control
public_reason: BLM Wyoming states cave resources are federally protected and may not be altered, damaged or removed.

entity_name: BLM Wyoming Cultural & Archaeological Materials — No Collection
public_reason: BLM Wyoming states archaeological and historic objects such as pottery, stone tools, arrowheads and historic remains are protected and cannot be collected without authorization.

entity_name: Wyoming Agate — Occurrence & Legal Research Hub
public_reason: WSGS confirms agate as a Wyoming gemstone/lapidary material; the hub intentionally provides no field collecting pin without site-level authority.

public_reason: WSGS confirms Wyoming diamond occurrence/exploration context; collecting rights and any prospective locality require separate current mineral-right verification.

entity_name: Wyoming Iolite, Sapphire & Ruby — Research Hub
public_reason: WSGS confirms these gemstone classes occur in Wyoming; no implied access, rights or collecting footprint is created.

entity_name: Wyoming Jade — Occurrence & Legal Research Hub
public_reason: Statewide geology hub separates verified jade occurrence literature from claim, mineral-estate and manager permission requirements.

entity_name: Wyoming Opal — Occurrence & Legal Research Hub
public_reason: WSGS confirms opal occurs in Wyoming; this page is occurrence education, not a collecting-location recommendation.

entity_name: Wyoming Peridot — Occurrence & Legal Research Hub
public_reason: WSGS confirms peridot occurs in Wyoming; exact lawful collecting localities require later site-specific resolution.

entity_name: Wyoming Petrified Wood — Occurrence & Legal Research Hub
public_reason: WSGS confirms petrified wood occurrence, while BLM applies a separate 25 lb plus one piece/day casual collection rule only where BLM land and local restrictions allow.

public_reason: Current BLM material explicitly names rockhounding and notes petrified wood and fossil occurrence. entity_name: Oregon Buttes WSA — Named BLM Rockhounding
public_reason: BLM currently names rock hounding as a recreation opportunity in this 5,700-acre WSA and reports no private/state inholdings. Existing mineral rights/claims, WSA constraints and current access still require trip-day screening.

entity_name: Red Creek Badlands WSA — Limited BLM Rockhounding
public_reason: BLM currently states rock hounding occurs on a limited basis. The WSA also includes state land and highly erodible terrain, so state-land authority, rights, disturbance and route conditions remain separate gates.

entity_name: South Pinnacles WSA — Rockhounding
public_reason: BLM explicitly lists rock hounding as a recreation opportunity, but motorized/mechanized travel is prohibited and the WSA is closed to mineral entry including gold panning; valid-existing-rights and trip-day access still require verification.

entity_name: The Pinnacles Geologic Site — BLM Rockhounding
public_reason: Current BLM site page explicitly lists rock hounding at this fee-free geologic site and provides the access route; active claims/private mineral interests still require material-matched rights screening.

entity_name: Whitehorse Creek WSA — Rockhounding
public_reason: The current BLM Whitehorse Creek WSA page describes badlands study, photography and bird watching but no longer names rockhounding. A prior named-activity signal is therefore tombstoned rather than treated as continuing collection authority.

entity_name: Yellowstone National Park — No Rock/Fossil Collection
public_reason: Yellowstone states that collecting natural resources, including rocks and fossils, is illegal.

entity_name: Big Cedar Ridge Fossil Site — Common Fossil Collection Class Guide

entity_name: Honeycombs WSA — Named BLM Rockhounding
